scope: Proposition 5.4 (Chronological partition input) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The cells and accounting classes described above can be constructed chronologically for every finite block. The construction preserves current-core equivariance, the cell spans and padding stated in (5.5) and the paragraph following it, all inherited accounting classes without splitting, and the property that one new cell meets at most one surviving old cell of each old child. After clipping, the raw cap per cell and remaining mask is N0. It supports the coarsening rule of Proposition 5.3 at each subsequent sparse step. Aside from the cap clipping separately bounded by (5.10), its total first-mass loss can be made arbitrarily small relative to the selected block mass by the fixed parameter cutoffs. An expected loss bound over the specified finite partition jitters suffices; the structural assertions and core equivariance hold for every realized construction. The comparison bounds apply to the actual running tables or to the nonnegative majorants indicated in their proofs.
